name: cboe_tail_hedge
claim: Buying options or protection loses money over time
tasty_value: Hedge costs (premium) can outweigh the protection and cap upside; hedging suits risk-averse investors
tasty_note: Qualitative; no tastylive figure for the cost of puts found.
our_value: PPUT trailed the S&P 500 TR by 3.5 pts/yr from 1988, 2.8 pts/yr from 2007, 3.0 pts/yr from 2016.
data: Cboe PPUT and CLL history CSVs; Yahoo ^SP500TR, ^IRX
method: As repro:cboe_short_vol. The matched mix is a monthly-rebalanced S&P 500 TR / T-bill blend with the stock weight chosen (0.5% grid) to match PPUT's 1988-2026 CAGR.
caveats: Gross index returns: no commissions, no bid-ask (Cboe indices trade at stated prices), no taxes. Real implementations lag the index.
Cboe publishes these indices and sponsored most of the early studies of them.
The S&P 500 TR comes from Yahoo ^SP500TR; Sharpe uses month-end returns and ^IRX, so it can differ by about +/-0.05 from other conventions.
PPUT buys a 5% OTM one-month put every month: one hedging design among many (tenor, strike and monetization rules change results a lot).
CLL's file starts 2008-08-26, so it has no full 2007 window.
The matched-mix drawdown is on month-end closes; PPUT's comparison number uses the same month-end basis.

claims.text: Buying options or protection loses money over time
claims.tasty_value: Hedge costs (premium) can outweigh the protection and cap upside; hedging suits risk-averse investors
claims.tasty_note: Qualitative; no tastylive figure for the cost of puts found.
claims.our_value: PPUT trailed the S&P 500 TR by 3.5 pts/yr from 1988, 2.8 pts/yr from 2007, 3.0 pts/yr from 2016.

claims.text: Long-volatility positions have no useful role in a portfolio
claims.tasty_value: Low IV rank favors long premium (debit spreads, long straddles); buy when IV rank and VIX are depressed
claims.tasty_note: tastylive gives long volatility a conditional role (low IV), not a hedge role.
claims.our_value: COVID peak-to-trough: PPUT -11.8% vs S&P 500 TR -33.8%; calendar 2020 PPUT 29.08% vs 18.40%; 2022 PPUT -19.81%.

claims.text: Manage risk by trading smaller rather than buying puts
claims.tasty_value: To reduce tail risk, cut position size first, prefer defined risk, and consider 60+ DTE; size each trade under about 5% of the account
claims.tasty_note: Agrees: tastylive's first lever is size, not puts.
claims.our_value: 1988-2026, a 56% S&P TR / 44% T-bill mix matches PPUT's 7.92% CAGR with a -31.5% max drawdown (month-end) vs PPUT -38.9%; worst month -9.4% vs -9.8%.
